verses.1: And David ran away from his enemies. He came forward and said, “In front of Jonathan, what have I done? What sins have I committed before your father? For I am seeking my own life.”
verses.2: And Hallelah said to him, “Do not do this! My father will not do anything great or small. He will not reveal this secret to me. How can he hide this from me? This is impossible.”
verses.3: And David sat down again, and he said, “My father knows that I have found your favor in your eyes. But Jonathan said, ‘Let it remain unknown, so that I will not be upset.’ But God lives, and your soul also lives, because you are my friend, just as the dead are friends with me.”
verses.4: And Jonathan said to David, “What shall your soul say, and what will I do for you?”
verses.5: And David said to Jonathan, “Now there’s a new month. I will go and sit down with the king for food. Then you can send me away, and I will hide in the field until morning.”
verses.6: If calamity befalls me, your father will say, “David shall go and ask for bread from me, for there is the offering of days there, for all the family.”
verses.7: If he says, “May good come to you,” then know that all evil will be taken away from him.
verses.8: And you have shown kindness to your servants, because in the covenant with Yahweh, you brought your servants along with you. But if there is any harm or danger to me, then you and your ancestors will be responsible for my death. Why do you bring me to such a fate?
verses.9: And Jonathan said to her, “Alas, for you! If I were to know that all this evil has come upon my father, and it will also come upon you, then I would not tell you.”
verses.10: And David said to Jonathan, “Who can tell me what your father has done that was so bad?”
verses.11: And Jonathan said to David, “Go out into the field.” So they went out into the field.
verses.12: And Jonathan said to David, “The LORD, the God of Israel, says that my father will be questioned soon. But now, it’s good for David. Not until then will I send for you. I’ve listened to your plea.”
verses.13: May Jehovah do thus to Jehonanah. May He also increase His favor upon me, as it pleases Him. I have turned your ear against you, and I have sent you away; but you went away to peace. May Jehovah be with you, just as He was with my father.
verses.14: And not if I am still alive. And may the LORD not show me any kindness or mercy.
verses.15: And you shall not remember your mercy in my house forever. Nor shall you remember that Jehovah has punished David’s enemies, every man from above the earth.
verses.16: And Johanan made peace with the house of David. He also asked Jehovah for help from those who were enemies of David.
verses.17: And Jonathan became the one who would bring David back to life through his love for him, just as his soul loved him.
verses.18: And Jehonatan said to him, “After a new month has begun, then you will be dismissed. For your ruler will be dismissed as well.”
verses.19: And three people will descend from above. You will come to the place where you were hidden on that day of the event. Then you will sit beside the stone that was there.
verses.20: And I am one of the three branches; I stand by to be sent forth into battle.
verses.21: And behold, I will send the boy to you. He will find the keys. If he says, “Here are the keys from you,” then take them and come back. It will be a relief for you, and there will be no more trouble from Jehovah.
verses.22: And if I say forever, then see: the gates are from you, and they will be with you always, because your Lord has sent them.
verses.23: And the words that I and you have spoken, behold, they are with God between me and you forever.
verses.24: And David hid himself in the field. Then, the new year began, and the king sat down at the crossroads to wait for his fate.
verses.25: And the king sat on his throne, once again. Then Jehonatan stood up and sat beside Shaul. He then took charge of the place where David was.
verses.26: And Shaul did not speak on that day, because he said that it was not clean. It wasn’t truly clean at all.
verses.27: And on the second day of the new month, David was appointed to lead the army. Shaul said to Jonathan, “Do you not know that neither Isai’s son will come here today? He will surely die.”
verses.28: And Jehonatan rebelled against Shaul. David asked him many questions from his seat in the house of bread.
verses.29: And he said, “Send me away, for there is a sacrifice to be offered for us in the city. My brother has ordered me to do this. Now, if I find favor in your eyes, then I will come and see my brother. But not yet; I will not go to the king’s palace.”
verses.30: And Sheol struck Jonathan, and he said to him, “Oh, I knew that you had chosen to be the son of Ishbi’ot, so that you could spread the evil of your mother’s name.”
verses.31: For all those days that Isaac lived on this earth, you and your kingdom will not be able to do anything. Now, send him to me, for he is a son of death.
verses.32: And Johanan rebelled against his father Shaul. He said to him, “Why have you died? What have you done?”
verses.33: Shaul took the spear upon himself to strike him. Yehonatan knew that it was all part of his father’s plan to kill David.
verses.34: And Jehonatan rose from his place at the table, with a broken jaw. He did not eat bread on the second day of that week, because he was sad over David’s death, as his father had said.
verses.35: In the morning, Jehonatan went to the place appointed by David. He was accompanied by a young boy.
verses.36: And he said to the boy, “Ruth, please find those half-books that I have left behind. The boy ran away, and he carried those half-books with him.”
verses.37: And the young man went to the place where Jehonatan had shot. Jehonatan called out to the young man, “Come here, you half-man!”
verses.38: And Jehovah Nathan called out to the boy quickly. He said, “Don’t stand up.” Then Jehovah Nathan took the instruments and went before his altar.
verses.39: And the boy would not know what it meant, but Jehovanathan and David knew what it meant.
verses.40: And Johanan gave all his possessions to the boy who belonged to him. He said to him, “Go and bring back the city.”
verses.41: The boy came, and David got up from his place. He threw earth over his face. He bowed down three times. Then each person kissed their neighbor. They wept for each other until David became proud.
verses.42: And Jonathan said to David, “Go and bless Shiloh, for we have chosen him as our king in the name of the LORD. May the LORD make it so that there will be peace between me and you, and between my descendants and your descendants, forever.”
